summary: Verified new Live RSA tracking (GET /api/incidents/{id}/rsa) and Customer reschedule (POST /api/incidents/{id}/reschedule) end-to-end. Backend pytest suite: 55/55 passing (7 new tests: rsa 404-when-no-dispatch, rsa progress advancement + linear coord interpolation over 6s with eta_min=10, reschedule success locks slot (locked=true, position=null, slot_start reflects requested time, timeline note 'Customer rescheduled'), reschedule rejects past/empty/no-slot (400 x3), and recompute_slots respects the lock — booking another slot at d_metro AFTER a customer lock does NOT move the locked incident's slot_start). Frontend Playwright on external REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL with seeded customer session cookie (test_session_fixed_ABC123): (a) HIGH incident detail after RSA dispatch renders rsa-tracker card with rsa-eta '9 min' and the progress bar advanced 1% -> 2% across a 5s poll cycle, current coord label rendered (37.7754, -122.4198 for d_metro origin). (b) LOW slot incident detail shows the appointment sentence with technician name + queue position, reschedule-time-input (datetime-local) and reschedule-btn; submitting a +3d future time shows the 'Appointment rescheduled' success toast. Full regression (auth, AI triage, photo upload, dealer ops assign/status/priority/escalate/resolve, KPIs, Connect sim, chat, callbacks, cron auth+flip, recordings, per-branch scoping, dealerships listing, dispatch workflow rsa/remote/slot, priority-ordered queue, lane distribution) still 100%.
critical_code_review_comments: reschedule endpoint doesn't validate the new time against business hours (BUSINESS_START_HOUR/END_HOUR) or dealership working days; a customer can lock a slot at 3am UTC. Consider snapping to _align_business() or 400-ing outside working hours.
reschedule endpoint doesn't check for double-booking conflicts on the same technician/lane. Two customers can lock overlapping slots for the same technician_id.

rsa_track hardcodes fallback origin=(37.77,-122.42) and dest = origin + (0.03,-0.025) when RSA record lacks origin/dest. For an incident dispatched before the origin/dest fields were persisted this yields SF coordinates — acceptable for the SIMULATION disclosure but worth surfacing in the RsaTracker UI as 'Simulated location'.
RsaTracker polls every 5s indefinitely once opened; after progress>=1 (status='arrived') the interval keeps firing. Stop the interval when arrived to save requests.

reschedule sets appointment.position=null but leaves appointment.lane and technician_id at their previous auto-assigned values. Since the slot is now user-chosen, lane/technician assignment could become stale relative to the actual queue; consider re-picking a lane at the requested time or marking as 'unassigned' until confirmed.

The customer datetime-local input is treated as local time and sent via new Date(rsWhen).toISOString(); this is correct, but there is no min= attribute on the input, so the browser doesn't prevent picking a past date client-side (backend does reject 400).
